intro: Write the equation, put in the numbers, then give the answer with its unit. Question 8 is a 6-mark answer.

questions.q: What is the unit of pressure?
questions.ms: Pa (pascal, N/m²).

questions.q: On a distance-time graph, a steeper straight line means the object is…
questions.ms: moving faster

questions.q: A runner completes 400 m in 50 s. Calculate the runner's average speed in m/s.
A train travels at an average speed of 80 km/h for 1.5 hours. How far does it travel, in km?
questions.ms: 120 km. M1 distance = speed × time, A1 80 × 1.5 = 120.

questions.q: A bus has an average speed of 30 km/h for a journey, but at one point its speedometer shows 50 km/h. Explain how both readings can be true.
questions.ms: 1 the speedometer shows instantaneous speed (at that moment); 1 the bus stops/slows at other times, so total distance ÷ total time is lower.

questions.q: Two trains move towards each other on parallel tracks, one at 60 km/h and the other at 40 km/h. What is their speed relative to each other, in km/h?
questions.ms: 100 km/h (moving towards each other, so add).

In which section is the dog moving fastest?
questions.ms: C (steepest line).

questions.q: Work out the dog's speed in section C, in m/s.
Work out the dog's average speed for the whole 30 seconds, in m/s.
Explain why a sharp knife cuts more easily than a blunt knife, and why a tractor has wide tyres for driving on soft, muddy fields. Use ideas about force, area and pressure.
questions.ms: Level 3 (5–6): both examples explained with pressure = force ÷ area. Level 2 (3–4): both described, one explained. Level 1 (1–2): simple statements. Points: pressure = force ÷ area; sharp knife has a very small area of contact; same force on a smaller area gives a larger pressure so it cuts through; tractor tyres have a large area; weight spread over a larger area gives a lower pressure; so the tractor does not sink into the mud.

questions.q: An elephant weighs 50 000 N. The total area of its feet touching the ground is 0.25 m<sup>2</sup>. Calculate the pressure on the ground in Pa.
questions.ms: 200 000 Pa. M1 pressure = force ÷ area, M1 50 000 ÷ 0.25, A1.

questions.q: A pressure of 2000 Pa acts on an area of 0.5 m<sup>2</sup>. Calculate the force in N.
questions.ms: 1000 N. M1 force = pressure × area, A1.

questions.q: Explain why a dam is built much thicker at the bottom than at the top.
questions.ms: 1 water pressure increases with depth; 1 more weight of water above pushing down; 1 so a bigger force acts on the bottom of the dam, which must be stronger.

questions.q: Use ideas about particles to explain how a gas exerts pressure on the walls of its container.
questions.ms: 1 gas particles move randomly / quickly; 1 they collide with the walls, exerting a force (on an area).

questions.q: A sealed can of gas is heated. Explain what happens to the pressure inside.
questions.ms: 1 particles move faster; 1 collide with walls more often / harder, so pressure increases.

questions.q: Explain why atmospheric pressure decreases as a plane climbs higher.
questions.ms: 1 less air above / smaller weight of air pushing down; 1 air is less dense, fewer particle collisions.

questions.q: A child of weight 300 N sits 2 m from the pivot of a seesaw. Calculate the moment of their weight, in N m.
questions.ms: 600 N m. M1 moment = force × distance, A1.

questions.q: A second child sits on the other side, 1.5 m from the pivot. The seesaw balances. Calculate the weight of the second child, in N.
questions.ms: 400 N. M1 anticlockwise moment = clockwise moment, M1 600 ÷ 1.5, A1.

questions.q: Explain why it is easier to open a door by pushing near the handle than near the hinge.
questions.ms: 1 handle is further from the pivot (hinge); 1 larger distance gives a larger moment for the same force.

questions.q: What does acceleration mean?
options: How much speed increases each second
questions.ms: How much speed increases each second.

questions.q: Ola drops a ball onto sand from different heights and measures the depth of each crater. Name the independent and dependent variables, and explain why a line graph is the right graph to draw.
questions.ms: 1 IV drop height; 1 DV crater depth; 1 both variables are continuous (numbers that can take any value), so a line graph.
